title: termal_spawn_session's 30 s bridge wait is shorter than the synchronous parent and child Engram binds it waits on
outcome: Found by the read-only dependency audit for w-33bee3bec3f0 (doubling the load-sensitive limits), Termal::Opus2, 2026-09-29, worktree at 515a90c. The MCP bridge posts spawn-session with the global TERMAL_DELEGATION_MCP_HTTP_TIMEOUT (30 s, delegation_mcp.rs:15; call at :947). The backend create_delegation calls bind_engram_delegation_best_effort (engram_host_adapter.rs:5477), which binds the parent and then the child in sequence, off the lock. One bind can spend the dispatch budget (status + checkpoint), then a 6 s work-binding read, then a bind at the call timeout, plus a stale retry. That is about 26–42 s worst case today, and about 46–72 s once the 10 s Engram deadlines become 20 s. Under load, the bridge can time out while the backend goes on to create and bind the child, so the caller sees a failure for a delegation that exists (compare w-4b192401033c). This predates w-33bee3bec3f0, which widens the gap. Fix directions: give the spawn call an allowance derived from the bind budgets plus the request timeout (as the source-root naming and acceptance calls already do), or move the binds out of the request path.
acceptance: termal_spawn_session's bridge wait exceeds the worst-case duration of the backend spawn request, including its synchronous parent and child Engram binds, as a relation stated in code (or the binds leave the request path); a test covers a spawn whose binds take longer than the old 30 s wait
